questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $x, y, z$~are in arithmetic progression, hence~$2y = x + z,$~also~\left|\begin{cases}3 & 4\sqrt{2} & x \\ 4 & 5\sqrt{2} & y \\ 5 & k & z\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Applying~${R}_{2} \to {R}_{1} + {R}_{3} - 2{R}_{2}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}3 & 4\sqrt{2} & x \\ 0 & k - 6\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 5 & k & z\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ ( k - 6\sqrt{2} ) ( 3z - 5x ) = 0$

$⇒ ( k - 6\sqrt{2} ) = 0$~or~$( 3z - 5x ) = 0$

If~$3z - 5x = 0$

$⇒ 3 ( x + 2d ) - 5x = 0$

$⇒ x = 3d$ (Not possible)

$⇒ k = 6\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ k^{2} = 72 .$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left|A\right| = \left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 4 + d & \left(sin\theta\right) - 2 \\ 1 & \left(sin\theta\right) + 2 & d \\ 5 & \left(2sin\theta\right) - d & \left(- sin\theta\right) + 2 + 2d\end{cases}\right|$

${R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - 2{R}_{2} + {R}_{1}$

$= \left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 4 + d & \left(sin\theta\right) - 2 \\ 1 & \left(sin\theta\right) + 2 & d \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$= 1\left\{\left(4 + d\right)d - \left(sin\theta + 2\right)\left(sin\theta - 2\right)\right\}$

$= 4d + d^{2} - \sin^{2}\theta + 4 = \left(d + 2\right)2 - \sin^{2}\theta$

We know that~$0 \le \sin^{2}\theta \le 1$

Given, the~minimum value of \left|A\right| = 8,$~which is possible, when~$\sin^{2}\theta = 1$

$⇒ \left(d + 2\right)2 = 9$

$⇒ d + 2 = \pm 3$

$⇒ d = 1$~or~$d = - 5 .$

Given the system of linear equations.

has infinitely many solutions, so

$D = \left|\begin{cases}8 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ \lambda & - 3 & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0 ⇒ \lambda = 4$

Also~${D}_{1} = {D}_{2} = {D}_{3} = 0$

${D}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \mu & - 3 & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0 ⇒ - 6 - 3\mu = 0$

So~$\mu = - 2$

Hence the point will be~ \left(4, - 2, - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

Now distance of point~ \left(4, - 2, - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$~from plane~$8x + y + 4z + 2 = 0$

$= \left|\dfrac{32 - 2 - 2 + 2}{{8}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {4}^{2}}\right| = \left|\dfrac{30}{9}\right| = \dfrac{10}{3}$

questions.q:
Let the system of linear equations

$x + y + kz = 2$

$2x + 3y - z = 1$

$3x + 4y + 2z = k$

have infinitely many solutions. Then the system

\left(k + 1\right)x + \left(2k - 1\right)y = 7$

\left(2k + 1\right)x + \left|k + 5\right|y = 10$& has :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Linear equations& $x + y + kz = 2$,~$2x + 3y - z = 1$~and~$3x + 4y + 2z = k$~have~infinitely many solutions.

Therefore,

\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & k \\ 2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(10\right) - 1\left(7\right) + k\left(- 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 10 - 7 - k = 0$

$⇒ 3 - k = 0$

$⇒ k = 3$

For $k = 3$,~the second system~of equations is

$4x + 5y = 7 \ldots \left(1\right)$

$7x + 8y = 10 \ldots \left(2\right)$

Clearly, they have a unique solution

Subtracting~ \left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$, we get

$3x + 3y = 3$

$⇒ x + y = 1

$

$\cos^{2} ⁡ \thetax + \left(1 + \sin^{2} ⁡ \theta\right)y + 4sin ⁡ 3\thetaz = 0$

\left|\begin{cases}1 + \cos^{2}\theta & \sin^{2}\theta & 4sin3\theta \\ \cos^{2}\theta & 1 + \sin^{2}\theta & 4sin3\theta \\ \cos^{2}\theta & \sin^{2}\theta & 1 + 4sin3\theta\end{cases}\right| = 0$

${R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - {R}_{2}$

\left|\begin{cases}1 + \cos^{2}\theta & \sin^{2}\theta & 4sin3\theta \\ \cos^{2}\theta & 1 + \sin^{2}\theta & 4sin3\theta \\ 0 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

${C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} + {C}_{1}$

\left|\begin{cases}1 + \cos^{2}\theta & 2 & 4sin3\theta \\ \cos^{2}\theta & 2 & 4sin3\theta \\ 0 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

${C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} + {C}_{3}$

Expanding along~${R}_{3}$

$⇒ \left(1 + \cos^{2}\theta\right)\left(2 + 4sin3\theta\right) - \left(2 + 4sin3\theta\right)\left(\cos^{2}\theta\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(2 + 4sin3\theta\right)\left(1 + \cos^{2}\theta - \cos^{2}\theta\right) = 0$

$⇒ sin3\theta = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ 3\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{18}$

questions.q: If the system of equations $2x + 3y - z = 0, x + ky - 2z = 0$ and $2x - y + z = 0$ has a non-trivial solution \left(x, y, z\right),$ then $\dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{y}{z} + \dfrac{z}{x} + k$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The system of equations& ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z = 0, {a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z = 0$~and~${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z = 0$~has a non-trivial solution, if~

\left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0 .$

Hence, for~the given lines~$2x + 3y - z = 0, x + ky - 2z = 0$~and~$2x - y + z = 0,$~we have

\left|\begin{cases}2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 1 & k & - 2 \\ 2 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(k - 2\right) - 3\left(1 + 4\right) - 1\left(- 1 - 2k\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2k - 4 - 15 + 1 + 2k = 0$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{9}{2}$

Thus, the lines are~

$2x + 3y - z = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

$x + $\dfrac{9}{2}$y - 2z = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

$2x - y + z = 0 . . . \left(3\right)$

\left($1\right) - \left(3\right) ⇒ 4y - 2z = 0$

$2y = z . . . \left(4\right)$

\dfrac{y}{z} = \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(5\right)$

put $z$ from eq~ \left($4\right)$~into~ \left($1\right)$

$2x + 3y - 2y = 0$

$2x + y = 0$

\dfrac{x}{y} = - \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left($6\right)$

From eq~ \left($4\right)$~and~ \left(6\right)$

$\dfrac{z}{x} = -4$

Hence,~$\dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{y}{z} + \dfrac{z}{x} +k = - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} -4 + \dfrac{9}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} .$

questions.q:
If the system of linear equations

$2x + 3y - z = - 2$

$x + y + z = 4$

$x - y + \left|\lambda\right|z = 4\lambda - 4$~where~$\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$,

has no solution, then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
If we have three equations in three variables,&

${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z = {d}_{1}{a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z = {d}_{2}{a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z = {d}_{3}$

then~$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$,${∆}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}{d}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {d}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {d}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$,${∆}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {d}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {d}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {d}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$,${∆}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {d}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {d}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {d}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$.

If the set of equations do not have a solution then~$∆ = 0$~and at least one among~${∆}_{1}, {∆}_{2}, {∆}_{3}$~is not equal to zero.

$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & - 1 & \left|\lambda\right|\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\lambda\right| =7 ⇒ \lambda = \pm7 \ldots \left(1\right)$

Case 1:~$\lambda = 7$

The system of equations are~

$2x + 3y - z = - 2x + y + z = 4x - y + 7z = 24$

$a \left(2x + 3y - z + 2\right) + b \left(x + y + z - 4\right) = \left(x - y + 7z - 24\right)$

Comparing the coefficients of~$x$~and~$y$~we get,~

$2a + b = 13a + b = - 1 ⇒ a = - 2, b = 5$

For these values of~$a$~and~$b$, coefficients of~$z$~and~the~constant~values are matching. So the set of equations will have infinitely many solutions.

Case 2:~$\lambda = - 7$

The system of equations are~

$2x + 3y - z = - 2x + y + z = 4x - y - 7z = - 32$

$a \left($2x + 3y - z + 2\right) + b \left($x + y + z - 4\right) = \left($x - y - 7z + 32\right)$

Comparing the coefficients of~$x$~and~$y$~we get,~

$2a + b = 13a + b = - 1 ⇒ a = - 2, b = 5$

For these values of~$a$~and~$b$, coefficients of~$z$& and& the& constant& values are not matching. So the set of equations will have no solutions.

$

questions.q: The greatest value of $c \in R$ for which the system of linear equations~$x - cy - cz = 0$,~$cx - y + cz = 0$,~$cx + cy - z = 0$& has a non-trivial solution, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∵$ System of equation has non trivial solution. It is possible only when~$∆ = 0$.
$∴ ∆ = \left|\begin{cases}1 & - c & - c \\ c & - 1 & c \\ c & c & - 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$
$⇒ 1\left(1 - c^{2}\right) + c\left(- c - c^{2}\right) - c\left(c^{2} + c\right) = 0$
$⇒ {2c}^{3} + 3c^{2} - 1 = 0$
$⇒ c = - 1, \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence,~the greatest value of $c = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: Consider the system of linear equation $x + y + z =4\mu, x + 2y + 2\lambdaz = 10\mu, x + 3y + 4{λ}^{2}z = {μ}^{2} + 15$, where $\lambda, \mu \in R$. Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?

The system is inconsistent if $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\mu \ne 1$

System of linear equations,

$⇒ $\Delta =$8{λ}^{2} - 6\lambda - 4{λ}^{2} + 2\lambda + 1$

$⇒ $\Delta =$4{λ}^{2} - 4\lambda + 1$

$⇒ $\Delta = ($2\lambda - 1{)}^{2}$

For unique solution, \Delta e$0$.

$⇒ 2\lambda - 1 e 0$

$⇒ \lambda e $\dfrac{1}{2}

Let, \Delta =$0, \lambda = $\dfrac{1}{2}

We know that, for infinite solutions, ${Δ}_{x} = {Δ}_{y} = {Δ}_{z} = 0$

$⇒ {Δ}_{x} = \left| egin{cases}$4\mu ext{ and } 1 ext{ and } 1 \ 10\mu ext{ and } 2 ext{ and } 1 \ {μ}^{2} + 15 ext{ and } 3 ext{ and } 1\end{cases} ight|$

$⇒ {Δ}_{x} = 4\mu \left($2 - 3 ight) - \left($10\mu - {μ}^{2} - 15 ight) + \left($30\mu - 2{μ}^{2} - 30 ight)$

questions.q:
Let the system of linear equations
$x + y + az = 2$

$3x + y + z = 4$

$x + 2z = 1$
have a unique solution \left(x, y, z\right)$. If \left(\alpha, x\right), \left(y, \alpha\right)$~and \left(x, - y\right)$ are collinear points, then the sum of absolute values of all possible values of $\alpha$& is

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,
$x + y + az = 2$

$3x + y + z = 4$

$x + 2z = 1$
Now finding,

$\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & \alpha \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - \left(\alpha + 3\right)$

${Δ}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}2 & 1 & \alpha \\ 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - \left(3 + \alpha\right)$

${Δ}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 2 & \alpha \\ 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - \left(\alpha + 3\right)$

${Δ}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$\alpha \ne - 3, x = \dfrac{△ 1}{△} = 1, y = \dfrac{△ 2}{△} = 1, z = \dfrac{△ 3}{△} = 0,$

Now points \left(\alpha, 1\right), \left(1, \alpha\right) \text{ and } \left(1, - 1\right)$ are collinear

\left|$\begin{cases}\alpha$& 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \alpha& 1 \\ 1 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \alpha\left(\alpha +1\right) - 1\left(1 - 1\right) + 1\left(-1 - \alpha\right) =0$

${α}^{2} + \alpha -1 - \alpha =0$

$\alpha = \pm1$

So,~\left|1\right| + \left|-1\right| = 2$

$

$2x + \alphay + 3z = 5$

$3x - y + \betaz = 3$

has infinitely many solutions, then $12\alpha + 13\beta$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

The system of linear equations

$x - 2y + z = - 4$,

$2x + \alphay + 3z = 5$ and

$3x - y + \betaz = 3$ has infinity many solutions,

So, $△ = {△}_{1} = {△}_{2} = {△}_{3}$

Now, finding,

${△}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}1 & - 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 3 & 3 & \beta\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 5\beta - 9 + 8\beta - 36 - 9 = 0$

$⇒ 13\beta = 54$

And, ${△}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}1 & - 2 & - 4 \\ 2 & \alpha & 5 \\ 3 & - 1 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 3\alpha + 5 + 12 - 30 + 8 + 12\alpha = 0$

$⇒ 15\alpha = 5$

$⇒ 12\alpha = 4$

Hence, the value of $12\alpha + 13\beta = 4 + 54 = 58$

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

System of linear equation,

$– x + 2y - 9z = 7 . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$– x + 3y + 7z = 9 . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

$– 2x + y + 5z = 8 . . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

$– 3x + y + 13z = \lambda . . . . . . \left($iv\right)$

Now solving, equations~ \left($i\right), \left($ii\right) \text{ and } \left(iii\right)$~we get,

$x = – 3, y = 2, z = 0$

Now substituting~in equation~ \left($iv\right)$~we get,

$3 $\times$3 + 2 = \lambda$

$⇒ \lambda = 11$

Now finding the distance of Point~ \left($– 3, 2, 0\right)$~from the plane~$2x - 2y + z = 11$~we get,

$d = \left|\dfrac{- 6 - 4 - 11}{{2}^{2} + {2}^{2} + 1}\right| = \dfrac{21}{3} =$7$

questions.q:
The ordered pair \left(a, b\right)$, for which the system of linear equations
$3x - 2y + z = b$

$5x - 8y + 9z = 3$

$2x + y + az = - 1$
has no solution, is

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given system of linear equations are
$3x - 2y + z = b$

$5x - 8y + 9z = 3$

$2x + y + az = - 1$

For system to have no solution,~

$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}3 & - 2 & 1 \\ 5 & - 8 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & a\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 3\left(- 8a - 9\right) + 2\left(5a - 18\right) + 1\left(21\right) = 0$

$⇒ a = - 3$

Also,~${∆}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}3 & - 2 & b \\ 5 & - 8 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = 3\left(5\right) + 2\left(- 11\right) + b\left(21\right) = 21b - 7$

If~$b = \dfrac{1}{3}$,~${∆}_{2} = 0$

So $b$~must be equal to~$- \dfrac{1}{3}$
